title: Types of muscle contraction

match.reason: The bank point defines concentric, eccentric and isometric contractions the same way the brief does, at a suitable Year 11 depth, and its terms and questions suit VCE Units 1 and 2, though it also covers agonist and antagonist roles that the brief does not mention.

confirm.reason: The bank point covers the whole muscular system, mainly agonist and antagonist pairs, with contraction types as only one part and only one question on them, so it is broader than this point on the three types of contraction.

draft.title: Types of muscle contraction
card: the muscle shortens while it produces force. The muscle pulls the joint through its movement against a load.
the muscle lengthens while it produces force. It controls a load by resisting it, such as slowing a weight as it is lowered.
the muscle produces force but stays the same length. There is no movement at the joint, such as holding a position still.
In all three types, the muscle is working. What differs is whether the muscle gets shorter, gets longer or stays the same length.
draft.remember: Concentric shortens, eccentric lengthens, isometric stays the same length.

a.q: Nina lowers a heavy box slowly onto the floor. The muscles at the front of her upper arm lengthen while they resist the weight. What type of contraction is this?
a.why: The muscle lengthens while it produces force to control the load, so the contraction is eccentric. It is not relaxed, because the muscle is working hard to slow the box.
a.clue: Does the muscle get shorter, longer or stay the same?

b.q: Tom holds a plank on a gym mat for 30 seconds. His abdominal muscles work hard, but he does not move. What type of contraction are they doing?
opts: Isometric, because the muscle length stays the same
Eccentric, because the muscle resists gravity
Concentric, because the muscle is producing force
No contraction, because there is no movement
b.why: The abdominal muscles produce force but stay the same length, so the contraction is isometric. The tempting answer is that no contraction occurs without movement, but a muscle can work hard with no movement at the joint.
b.clue: Check whether the muscle changes length while it works.

b.best: Isometric, because the muscle length stays the same
